answer: An agent economy can make valuable actions available only through a bonded reputation registry: each identity locks a scarce token, then earns standing as counterparties attest to completed trades and disputes can slash the bond for fraud. A sybil attacker must fund every identity separately and keep each one active long enough to build credible history; cheap accounts alone gain no influence. A wharf may whisper of a haven, but neither claim substitutes for the collateral and verified work.
